chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Uthman ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Ajlan said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Be good to the beasts of burden.' I asked: 'And what is good treatment of the beasts of burden?' He said: 'Gratitude to the One who bestowed them, and fulfilling their rights.'

key_terms.جِوَارُ النَّعَمِ: Good treatment of beasts of burden

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of good treatment (husn al-jawar) for animals according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines 'good neighborliness' (*husn al-jawar*) of animals not merely as physical care, but as a spiritual act of gratitude (*shukr*) to the Divine Giver and the fulfillment of their specific rights (*huquq*). This concept elevates animal welfare from a social courtesy to a theological obligation, linking the treatment of creation directly to the believer's relationship with God.
